meta.ci_method: percentile bootstrap over replications; differences are paired by replication (common random numbers)

parameters.source: assumed, no public source for a same-day backfill probability of a screening colonoscopy no-show. Anchors: E12-1 lists a unit that reached a 98% replacement rate for cancellations with a formal 'fill every slot' agreement (cancellations with notice, not same-day no-shows), and a survey that found services 'striving' to backfill; no-shows are found out too late to refill most of the time, so a low value is used.
Switch: the layer is on when this file is loaded.

assumed, no public source. Three endoscopy providers share the cohort; the pathway's referral attempts go to providers endoscopy-0, endoscopy-1, ..., and a case's first referral goes to provider (case index mod 3).
Multiplier on the slot supply, 1.0 = base capacity. The capacity sensitivity of results.md sets it to 0.70, 0.85, 1.00 and 1.15.

Calibrated so that the BASELINE arm fills about 87% of the offered slots over the utilisation window (the 80-90% the ticket asks for; the unit-level utilisation target the NHS programme quotes is 90-95%, E12-1). One session is 6 colonoscopies. No public figure gives the sessions a catchment of positive-FIT patients needs; this is a scale device, stated, not a measurement.

NHS Improving Quality, The Productive Endoscopy Unit - Scheduling (v1), docs/evidence.md section 12 (E12-1): a four-hour session is 12 points at 1 point = 15 minutes of session time, and a colonoscopy is 2 points (E12-2, JAG points guidance), so a fully trained endoscopist does 6 colonoscopies per session. Training lists (8 points) give 4.
Same figure as O_ACCEPT_ESC_SUPERVISOR and O_ACCEPT_ESC_COORDINATOR in simulator/sim/effort.py (assumed: 2 minutes to open the case, read the context and accept); a test keeps the two equal.

7.2 minutes for the phone call (sourced-adjacent: Heslop 2014 follow-up call, O'Leary 2023 call logs, docs/evidence.md E11-1 and E11-2) plus 1.5 minutes to approve the drafted message (assumed): O_SUPERVISOR_CALL/O_COORDINATOR_CALL plus O_APPROVE_DRAFT in simulator/sim/effort.py; a test keeps them equal. Charged when the escalation is one that asks the patient to act.

Calibrated like the supervisor's budget, for the programme coordinator (second rung of the escalation ladder and watchdog flags): unconstrained demand 90 minutes per day per 1,000 cases at 85%, which is 0.25 of a full-time person at 6 productive hours a day.
Multiplier on both staff budgets, 1.0 = base staffing. The staffing sensitivity of results.md sets it to 0.50, 0.75, 1.00 and 1.50.

Calibrated: the supervisor's daily minutes budget per 1,000 cases, set so that the unconstrained demand on the supervisor in the literature-anchored scenario (the scenario to quote) is about 85% of the budget over the utilisation window (demand 45 minutes per day per 1,000 cases at 85%). 45 minutes per day per 1,000 cases is 0.125 of a full-time person at 6 productive hours a day. No public staffing ratio exists for a result-tracking programme (docs/evidence.md section 11.3).

Definition, not evidence: utilisation is measured up to day 150, the period in which about 90% of the baseline arm's appointments fall in the unconstrained model (the 90th percentile of appointment day is day 147 at base parameters). The same window measures the staff budgets' utilisation.

Definition, not evidence: utilisation is measured from day 30 of the run. Results arrive over the first 30 days and the median booking lead is 24 days, so before day 30 hardly anyone can hold a booking and counting those empty slots would only understate utilisation (day 34 is the 10th percentile of appointment day in the unconstrained baseline arm at base parameters).
